modern: From Catulus, not to be indifferent when a friend finds fault, even if he should find fault without reason, but to try to restore him to his usual frame of mind; and to be ready to speak well of teachers, as is said of Domitius and Athenodotus; and to love my children truly.
original: From Catulus not to be indifferent when a friend finds fault, even if he should find fault without reason, but to try to restore him to his usual disposition; and to be ready to speak well of teachers, as it is reported of Domitius and Athenodotus; and to love my children truly.
